boundary: No on-land surface rupture: the Mw 7.8 (USGS us6000tkt2, 15 Aug 2026 05:58 WITA) broke the south-dipping Flores back-arc thrust offshore, ~20-25 km north of the Nagekeo coast (USGS epicentre -8.336, 121.345; BMKG '30 km NE of Mbay'). The expected NISAR signal is broad hanging-wall uplift of the north Nagekeo coast (Aesesa, Wolowae) fading southward, with local decorrelation where the ground failed (cracks and hot-water spouts at Tonggurambang) and the tsunami swash zone (Anakoli beach). Damage inside the ±40 km window is shaking damage scattered across Nagekeo, including the south coast, and does not follow one sharp line. The worst-hit regencies (Manggarai, East Manggarai: 75 of ~103 deaths by 25 Aug) and Kelimutu, Maumere and Mauponggo all lie outside the window.

items.title: Ground cracks spouting hot water at Tonggurambang
items.place: Dusun Muara, Desa Tonggurambang (OSM 'Tonggu Rambang'), Kecamatan Aesesa, Nagekeo, north coast
items.what_it_shows: TribunFlores report (visited 17 Aug 2026): during the 15 Aug quake the ground around homes in Dusun Muara cracked and hot water spouted from the cracks, in places from inside a house. Villagers showed the reporter the cracks and the rubble of a collapsed house. The spouting stopped after an aftershock. This is ground failure ~19 km south of the USGS epicentre: the most NISAR-relevant ground report in the window.
items.notes: Point is the OSM village node 'Tonggu Rambang' (place=village); the exact dusun/crack location is not given. The article names the resident quoted; deliberately not repeated here. Likely liquefaction or a disturbed hot spring on the coastal plain; that interpretation is ours, not the source's.

items.title: Five houses wrecked in Aeramo, Dusun V
items.place: Dusun V (RT 21 and RT 33), Desa Aeramo, Kecamatan Aesesa, Nagekeo
items.what_it_shows: FloresPos (15 Aug 2026, reporter on site): five houses in Dusun V of Aeramo were heavily damaged, with cracked walls, collapsed roofs and broken support posts, and are uninhabitable. Residents, especially women and children, fled to the hills and were sleeping in the open for fear of aftershocks.
items.notes: Point is the OSM Aeramo village node, ~6 km SE of Mbay; Dusun V is not mapped. The article lists homeowners' names; deliberately omitted. ~29 km S of the USGS epicentre, on the hanging wall.

items.title: Tsunami hits a 356-pupil scout camp on the beach at Kota Jogo, Anakoli
items.place: Kota Jogo beach, Desa Anakoli, Kecamatan Wolowae, Nagekeo, north coast
items.what_it_shows: Vokal Publika (teacher interviewed 21 Aug 2026): about 356 pupils from five primary schools and SMP Satap Anakoli were camped ~10 m from the shoreline when the quake struck at ~06:00. The only exit was a lane between barbed-wire fences, and children were trampled or cut pushing through. About 10 minutes later the sea rose an estimated 1.5 m over the site. About 20 people had light injuries; no one died. Wikipedia's article (citing this) says several people were swept away but survived.
items.notes: Point is the OSM Anakoli village node; the Kota Jogo beach campsite itself is not mapped and may be up to a few km from it on the coast. The 1.5 m wave height is a teacher's estimate, not a survey value (the post-event survey maxima of 2.4-2.7 m were at villages in Manggarai/East Manggarai, outside this window). A named teacher is quoted in the source; omitted here.

items.title: Degalea, on the south coast: 60 houses and two schools heavily damaged
items.place: Desa Degalea, Kecamatan Nangaroro, Nagekeo (south side of Flores)
items.what_it_shows: Ekora NTT (18 Aug 2026), quoting the village secretary: more than 80 houses and public buildings were damaged, including 60 houses heavily damaged. The SDI Lea and SDK Wolofeo school buildings, two kindergartens, two places of worship and the village office were heavily damaged. Two people were seriously injured and referred to RSUD Bajawa. No one died. Residents moved into four village camps. The village is ~52 km SSW of the USGS epicentre, across the island from the rupture: heavy damage far from the fault.
items.notes: Point is the OSM Degalea village node; the two schools are not mapped. Nearby Mauponggo (300 houses heavily damaged; Puskesmas, camat office and BRI unit badly damaged, per TribunFlores 18 Aug) lies ~3 km south of the window edge (-8.890, 121.211), so it is not included as an item. A named resident is quoted in the source; omitted here.

items.title: RSUD Ende: patients moved into tents as a precaution
items.what_it_shows: Kompas (15 Aug 2026): 70 inpatients and eight perinatal babies at RSUD Ende were moved out of the wards after the shaking, and 15 patients and five babies were then cared for in emergency tents in the hospital grounds as a precaution against aftershocks. Police also set up shelter tents on the Polres Ende field. Neither article reports structural damage to the hospital. Ende town, ~66 km SE of the epicentre, is the control: strong shaking, a scare and an evacuation, but no reported ground failure.
items.credit: Seraphinus Sandi Hayon Jehadu, Ihsanuddin / Kompas.com
items.notes: Coordinates are the OSM hospital point (amenity=hospital). Earlier article with the 70-patient figure: https://regional.kompas.com/read/2026/08/15/121834178/gempa-m-77-guncang-flores-pasien-rsud-ende-dan-maumere-dievakuasi. 'Unaffected' means no damage reported at this site; it does not mean undamaged. Ende Regency recorded 3 deaths (BNPB via Antara, 25 Aug), and landslides cut the Ende-Nagekeo road. The point is ~1 km inside the window's southern edge.
